## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred; Miller, Edward Leopold; Miller, Mrs Altmann [12. März 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.104
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.104
- Datum: 12.3.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 5 Scans

pages.transcription:
Newhaven Hotel Taft 12 March. Dear Hannah and Manfred, we had
today your letter from the 27. February - very quick, but mail is not
regularly at all. On the other hand your letter N° 3, which you answered
in your letter N° 4 as commercial[?] never arrived and it seems that you did not get our first
letters from Newyork about your daughter. There are now delays - The weather
is terrific, snowstorms and blizzards and furthermore we are in war.
Lotte behaves very badly against me. She knows that I have retired to New-
haven for work and instead of helping me she gets asthma-attacks and now
a thick influenza so that I, poor chap, have to care for her. I hope she will
be able to leave the bed tomorrow. In any case she must be careful as the
weather is disgusting, sharp winds blowing with ice and rain, the streets so
muddy that I who hate this since my early childhood has to buy rubbers.
Newhaven is a little place, not nice and one is lost in an American
little town without a car. If we are invited one has to bring us back as
there are not many busses - it is understood, that even a poor man has
his car in America (except in New York where it is paradoxically imprac-
ticable). The advantages are 1/ the library of the University, I can take
as many books at home as I want and go to the shelves myself, and that
is for me a delight as I have been without books for nearly a year
2/ I am not bothered by all this people which is now crowded in Newyork
- the whole Vienna, Berlin, Paris, Frankfurt and all horrible towns. So
I have time to work and even to think. 3/ We have opportunity to see
those who are real good friends quietly. There was Shalom Asch here,
Joachim Maass, Jules Romains, Bertolt Viertel, Friday comes Van Loon,
you see a very good choice 4/ it is altogether cheaper: not the Hotel,
which I do not like very much but all the daily expenses and the
Schnorrers. I do here some little work and prepare for the greater one
which I will write in Rio if we should return there. Nothing is sure
and we make no plans. America has its advantages - libraries,
possibilities of income and - and Brazil - beauty, quiet life. Our de-
cision depends from so many things, especially the developments in the
world. Everyones life is but a microbe in this monsters body which we
call: the War, shall we ever see a more sensible mankind?
Now to your pet! I have sincerely the conviction that Eva could not have
been better placed than at Mrs Schaeffer. It is just what I liked for her,
a modest surrounding without luxury, a careful and intelligent person who
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf zwei Seiten (hier Seite 1). Violette Tinte. Sehr gut lesbar.

pages.transcription:
understands children and is nearer to our own conceptions of education
good company and - if this terrific winter ends - a beautiful surrounding.
You may understand that we have been ourselves anxious the first days
if she would like it and we enjoy it very much that she seems to be
happy as possible. We all together have pressed her very hard to write
more substantially to you because I understand that you like just to
hear the little trifles of her daily life. I do not want to make a pro-
fessional writer out of her but she is now in the age where she could
learn to talk also with the pen to her mother. And she must under-
stand that you are waiting miles and miles away for every word from
her and that she should therefore give a little push to her brain to write more
than a few quick words - I can imagine so well how you open her letters
and in midst of your joy (and your tears) wishing they should contain
somewhat more of her.
From England I had except of Friedentals letter not a single one
for months and months. I know nothing what happens. As to material
things I shall have to make a tax report very soon, but I do not know
what came in from literary sources all this year. I will write about all this to my accountant
and give you a copy of it, so that you make it with him together, as
far as we can - I carry no files and no accounts here. But I will pre-
pare everything. Here I hope to come through - I could have some
wellpaid articles but I prefer to continue my own work and let these
possibilities always open. Would it not be for the exterior things we
would continue here our quiet and modest life - I want no publicity,
no more big towns and noisy pleasures. The only thing everybody of us
would like most of all - security! - seems to be gone for our genera-
tion and we must learn to ride on the waves. Now nothing more
then kindest regards to all! Yours ever

Stefan

Dear Mr Miller I heard with great pleasure that you
feel allright again. How often are we remembering the
garden and how beautiful it will be in spring. Unfortunately
there is now no possibility to return as we hoped - no passages
for months! But let us hope the best! Kindest regards
Stefan Zweig
pages.notes: Zweite Seite des Briefes. Am linken Rand befindet sich eine vertikale Anmerkung: 'Please, Manfred, stay at Bath! We feel much better knowing both of you there in midst of the quiet meadows!'
